top_violation_types.title: Prohibited Punishments - No Harsh, Cruel or Unusual (26 TAC §746.2805)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Two caregivers were observed administering prohibited punishment. One caregiver was observed pulling a child by the arm from underneath a table and another caregiver was observed grabbing a child by the arm and holding onto the child to keep the child from moving out of a chair. The same caregiver was observed grabbing on a child and pulling on the child's arms.

top_violation_types.title: Measurement of Use Zone for Slides - in Front of Access and on Sides (26 TAC §746.4805(a))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The use zone for the slides lacked the required perimeter.

top_violation_types.title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The ground is splitting open and causing a tripping hazard at the entrance to the playground.       Photos taken

top_violation_types.title: Fenced Outdoor Activity Space -Gates Locked (26 TAC §746.4309)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The fence gate had a locked placed and 3 zip ties.  The lock was opened, except, the gate could not be opened as the zip ties were attached holding the gate to the post.  The zip ties were removed during the inspection.

top_violation_types.title: Required Admission Information - Physician Information (26 TAC §746.605(11))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: 1 child needs emergency care authorization to be redone due to water damage on form.

top_violation_types.title: Documentation of Fire Inspection (26 TAC §746.5103)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The fire inspection report was not available for review.

top_violation_types.title: Children Handwashing After Feeding or Touching Animals (26 TAC §746.3417(6))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The children were finishing up their lunch when I got to the location. As they finished up, they were directed to get their napmats and lay down for nap.

top_violation_types.title: AP Report Child Injury Requiring Medical Treatment by a Health-Care Professional or Hospitalization (26 TAC §746.305(a)(2))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: During the investigation, it was determined that the staff was aware of a child receiving medical attention after sustaining an injury while in care, but did not report to Child Care Licensing within two days of becoming notified.
